items.title: The iPhone Duo feels far more intuitive with Apple’s new face unlock
items.summary: Apple is testing a simplified face unlock on the iPhone Duo, improving speed and comfort over Touch ID while keeping some security limits.
items.excerpt: Apple is testing adding face unlock to the iPhone Duo - not true Face ID, but something a little simpler and less secure. So far, it works great, and even with a few Apple-imposed security limitations, it makes the Duo quicker and more comfortable to use than relying on Touch ID every time. That's one of my gripes with the phone taken care of. The Duo's foldable architecture means that Apple couldn't fit in the full…
items.whyItMatters: Tech users will appreciate faster, easier access on a foldable device, though security trade‑offs remain.

items.title: This tiny gamepad with dual analog thumbsticks pushes the limits of portable controllers
items.summary: The article reviews a compact dual-analog thumbstick gamepad that rivals larger controllers in functionality for portable use.
items.excerpt: As much as I appreciate the ingenious design of the Nintendo Switch's Joy-Con, my family and I can't stand using them as standalone gamepads. So when we travel with the Switch 2, we always bring at least one full-size gamepad, plus a couple of 8BitDo's Zero 2 controllers for games that don't use analog thumbsticks. I've spent years hunting for an alternative that pairs the size of the Zero 2 with as much of the…
items.whyItMatters: It offers a smaller, more ergonomic alternative for tech-savvy gamers seeking portability without sacrificing control.

items.title: My favorite recipe app just got a big upgrade — and a subscription fee
items.summary: Paprika 4, a recipe‑management app, launches with extensive upgrades and a new subscription model across all platforms.

I tested Paprika 4 for several weeks while it was in open beta, and the update recently launched across Android (the version I've been using), iOS, Windows, and macOS. items.whyItMatters: Tech users will see new features and pay‑wall changes that affect app usage and budgeting.

Unfortunately, its privacy reputation led to the "pervert glasses" moniker. Smart glasses have never been more unpopular. items.title: Apple’s HomeView is my new favorite smart display — but not my daughter’s
items.summary: Apple’s HomeView smart display excels at home control, kitchen use, audio, and photo display, featuring Siri AI but with occasional slowness.

It's superb at controlling my smart home; it's an excellent hands-free kitchen companion, a good speaker, and a gorgeous digital photo frame.
